text: dsh-orchestrator 是面向 DeepSeek Harness 的本地任务看板插件，在 Web 客户端提供项目与 issue 看板，并通过工具、命令和 RPC 共享同一套任务数据。它按工作区隔离项目，支持创建和筛选 issue、评论与活动记录、状态和优先级管理、定时规则、自动从待办队列调度并为每项工作创建独立会话。agent 可列出、读取、更新、评论和提议任务，也可运行分轮规划；提议、验收和归档由用户控制。适合在 DSH 中组织代码工作和审核 agent 产出的任务；需要 DSH 的存储、工具、agent 与 Web 服务组件，不需额外 API key。

dsh-orchestrator is a local issue board for DeepSeek Harness. Its web panel organizes workspace tasks; tools and /task let agents manage and propose issues. A scheduler starts prioritized work in fresh sessions; a planning loop processes the queue. Users approve proposals and accept results.

dsh-orchestrator 的功能「workspace-board」：按工作区展示项目任务，支持在浏览器看板查看并编辑 issue。
dsh-orchestrator 的功能「agent-tools」：agent 可通过工具筛选任务、读取详情、更新状态、评论和提议 issue。
dsh-orchestrator 的功能「scheduler」：调度器按优先级启动待办任务，为每项任务创建会话并支持 cron。
dsh-orchestrator 的功能「planning」：规划工具按轮次调用新 agent 处理现有任务队列，并受轮数上限约束。

@ericjiang0423/dsh-orchestrator README · Features：| Feature                  | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| One Board Per Repository | The board is bound to the session's working directory, not to the conversation: two sessions in the same repo share a board, and a session in another repo sees its own — the host resolves it, so the browser can never mix projects                                               |
| Fresh Session Per Issue  | "Work on this" opens a brand-new session with the issue's brief and binds the issue to it, so every issue's transcript and cost are its own — and several can run at once

@ericjiang0423/dsh-orchestrator README · Install from source (recommended)：Clone, build, and link the checkout into the profile. `dsh plugin add .` from inside the checkout registers the local build, so later `npm run build` runs are picked up without reinstalling:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/EricJiang0423/dsh-orchestrator.git
cd dsh-orchestrator
npm install && npm run build
dsh plugin --profile web add .

@ericjiang0423/dsh-orchestrator README · Install from source (recommended)：`lib/` is gitignored build output. `npm test` builds it automatically when it is missing (a `pretest` hook runs `npm run build` first), so on a fresh clone you can run tests right after `npm install` without building by hand. Once `lib/` exists, `npm test` skips the rebuild to stay fast — run `npm run build` explicitly to test your latest source changes.

@ericjiang0423/dsh-orchestrator README · Install from npm (registry)：> ⚠️ The unscoped `dsh-orchestrator` on the registry belongs to an unrelated project (zibo/dsh-agent-mesh). This project is published under a scope:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add @ericjiang0423/dsh-orchestrator
```

@ericjiang0423/dsh-orchestrator README · Architecture：```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': {'fontSize': '14px'}}}%% graph LR UI[Board View
React] -->|RPC + SSE| SVC[Taskboard Service

@ericjiang0423/dsh-orchestrator README · Architecture：The browser half never talks to storage directly. Every read and write goes through `ctx.taskboard`, whether the caller is the board's own RPC route, a model-facing tool, the planning loop, or the scheduler — so the two human gates (no self-approval, no self-acceptance) live in one place and apply to every caller. The scheduler is the only thing that starts work on its own, and it draws exclusively from `todo`, which only a human can put an issue into.

---

@ericjiang0423/dsh-orchestrator README · Configuration：| Key                         | Default | Description                                                                                                                  |
| --------------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `scheduler.concurrency`     | `1`     | How many issues may run at once; changeable live from the board header                                                       |
| `scheduler.autoPull`        | `true`  | Whether the board pulls from `todo` on its own; changeable live from the board header                                        |
| `scheduler.sweepIntervalMs` | `30000` | Safety-net sweep that frees slots occupied by vanished sessions                                                              |
| `plan.subagentProvider`     | `spawn` | Fresh structured-output subagent provider used for every planning round                                                      |
| `plan.maxRounds`            | `32`    | Default AND ceiling for one `taskboard_plan` run; a call may lower it, never raise it

@ericjiang0423/dsh-orchestrator README · API：The browser half talks to the host half over one endpoint, `POST /_dsh/taskboard/rpc`, with `{ method, params }` in the body, rather than one REST path per resource. DeepSeek Harness's typed RPC layer requires build-time code generation this plugin's build does not run, so the route is deliberately explicit — see [docs/spike-findings.md](docs/spike-findings.md) for why.

@ericjiang0423/dsh-orchestrator README · API：| Method                | Description                                                                                    |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `board.view`          | The board this session belongs to (resolved from its workspace), with live scheduler state     |
| `project.list`        | List every project                                                                             |
| `project.create`      | Create a project                                                                               |
| `task.list`           | List issues, optionally filtered by project, status, or session                                |
| `task.get`            | Read one issue with its comments and activity trail                                            |
| `task.create`         | Create an issue                                                                                |
| `task.update`         | Change an issue; refuses a stale `expectedVersion`                                             |
| `comment.create`      | Add a comment to an is
